rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Stress** $\sigma = F/A$ (Pa) is force per unit area; **strain** $\epsilon = \Delta L/L$ is the dimensionless fractional deformation; **Young's modulus** $Y = FL/(A\Delta L)$ is their ratio within the elastic limit. Elasticity means full shape recovery on unloading; plasticity means permanent deformation.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Stress-Strain vs Force-Extension:** Stress-strain curves are material properties (independent of geometry), while force-extension curves depend on the specific sample's dimensions. $E = \sigma/\varepsilon$ is a material constant; $k = F/x$ depends on length and cross-section.  ·  **Linear Region Constraint:** The linear proportionality $\sigma = E\varepsilon$ (Hooke's law) holds *only* up to the proportional limit. Beyond this, the curve is non-linear even before the elastic limit (where full recovery still occurs). The elastic limit and proportional limit are close but distinct.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Strain is dimensionless — never attach units.  ·  Stress and pressure share the N/m² unit but are different concepts (internal vs external).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Stress is not force:** it is force divided by area — a thin wire breaks under the same force that a thick rod survives.  ·  **Strain is dimensionless** — a ratio of like quantities.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Calculate stress, strain and Young's modulus for a loaded wire with correct unit conversions.  ·  Label all six regions on a mild steel stress–strain curve.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m² — the #1 conversion trap."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A wire of length 3 m and radius 0.5 mm extends 1.5 mm under 200 N. Find Y.** — A = πr² = 7.85×10⁻⁷ m²; Y = FL/(AΔL) = 200×3/(7.85×10⁻⁷×1.5×10⁻³) = 600/1.18×10⁻⁹ = 5.1×10¹¹ Pa.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Definitions repeat (2023, 2024); numericals appear nearly every year — practise all three patterns.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Stress and strain belong to the material;** force and extension belong to the specimen — that is why engineers tabulate Y, not k.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: σ = F/A (Pa); ε = ΔL/L (dimensionless); Y = σ/ε = FL/(AΔL).  ·  Elasticity = regains shape; plasticity = keeps deformed shape.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Steel's Y ≈ 2×10¹¹ Pa; copper's ≈ 1.1×10¹¹ Pa; human bone ≈ 1.6×10¹⁰ Pa.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — How Materials Respond to Load Pull on any solid and it deforms. Stress normalises the pull by area, strain normalises the deformation by size — together they describe the *material*, not the specimen. Their ratio is Young's modulus, and their graph tells the whole story from elastic stretch to fracture.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Definitions **Stress:** force per unit area acting on a body. $$\sigma = \frac{F}{A} \quad \text{(N/m}^2 = \text{Pa)}$$ Types: **longitudinal (tensile/compressive)**, **shear** (tangential force), **volume (bulk)** (uniform pressure). **Strain:** the fractional deformation produced — dimensionless.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 38:** $k = YA/L$ — object stiffness from material stiffness. - **To Topic 41:** Poisson's ratio links lateral to longitudinal strain. - **Stress–strain graph regions:** proportional limit (Hooke) → elastic limit → yield → ultimate stress → fracture.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Ductile vs Brittle Failure Mode:** Ductile materials have a significant plastic region (yield, strain hardening, necking) and fracture after large deformation. Brittle materials fracture near the elastic limit with little/no plastic deformation — no warning before failure.  ·  The elastic limit is the maximum stress from which the body still recovers fully.  ·  For safety design, working stress is kept well below the yield/ultimate stress (safety factor).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: NEB frequently asks to label the stress–strain curve and to calculate E from a numerical.  ·  Verified PYQs: definitions (2023, 2024 — 3m); steel-wire numerical (2022, 2024 — 3m); copper-wire Y (2020 — 4m); cable mass (2024 — 3m).  ·  "Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain within the elastic limit."
